note: Flat faces of the Nezu fanghe (KIT.md § Flat faces), from the project owner's phone photographs through the vitrine glass (1536 × 2048, no larger originals). Vessel frame: mm, Y up, front (+Z) = the HANDLE face. The lobed faces are not planes: each lobe bows ≈ 7 mm proud of the corner plane and the crease between two lobes runs ≈ 13 mm behind it, so every lobe face is flattened onto the CORNER plane (|x| or |z| = 105) and features away from the corners shift by up to a few mm with the camera's obliquity. Points are [photo px x, y, vessel x, y, z]: corner-flange roots at register borders (frieze top y 297, frieze/lobe border y 255, lobe bottom y 130) — the only in-plane landmarks these faces have.

p25.note: handle (+Z) face, lobes and frieze, close, from the left; ≈ 4 px/mm

p42.note: right (+X) face, handle on the left, ≈ 20° elevated, ≈ 2.3 px/mm

p45.note: handle (+Z) face close-up: horns, head, frieze, upper lobe masks; ≈ 6 px/mm

face-front.label: handle face (+Z): frieze and lobe masks (y 120–305)
face-front.trust: approximate: vessel A. Photo 25 is close and from the upper left, so the right lobe (x > 0) is read nearly head-on and is the tracing source; the left lobe is oblique and its lower part curves away from the corner plane (its eye lands ≈ 20 mm high). The handle's body covers the centre. Read on a 5 mm grid to ± 2 mm.
face-front.fit: least-squares fit of the points: rms 0.69 mm, max 1.21 mm (tools/faces.mjs --rectify prints it)

face-side.label: right face (+X): frieze and lobe masks (y 120–305)
face-side.trust: fair: vessel A, both lobes nearly symmetric in the flattening; ≈ 2.3 px/mm, soft. The V between the lobes and the crease are read here.
face-side.fit: least-squares fit of the points: rms 1.27 mm, max 2.37 mm
